 United's Chelsea test could make or break Carrick
 Published : 31 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 31 October 2026, 13:51
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Agencies 
 Photo: Reuters 
 Michael Carrick's future at Manchester United is increasingly uncertain, and Saturday's trip to Chelsea could prove decisive in determining how much longer he remains in the dugout. Eight games without a win have left the Englishman under mounting pressure, with his side struggling to produce both results and convincing performances. 
 The energy and organisation that characterised his interim spell last season have given way to a team seemingly short of direction and identity. United have slipped to 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation zone, and their latest defeat, a 3-0 loss to Bournemouth at Old Trafford, has intensified scrutiny of Carrick's position.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 The club have given him at least one more opportunity to turn things around, but the challenge at Stamford Bridge will be considerable. Beyond ending the winless run, Carrick must find solutions to problems that have become increasingly apparent in United's approach. Four areas, in particular, demand attention.
 Make United harder to play through 
 One of United's biggest problems has been their inability to make an aggressive pressing approach work. The intention to win possession high up the pitch is understandable, but poor coordination and a lack of compactness have repeatedly left them vulnerable.
 United have employed a high block in 36 per cent of opposition build-up phases this season, making them one of the Premier League's most frequent users of the approach. Only Tottenham and Liverpool have done so more often, with Manchester City level with United.
 However, the numbers suggest that the strategy has delivered little attacking reward. United have won possession high up the pitch 52 times, but only 10 of those recoveries have resulted in a shot. They are yet to score from such situations.
 Defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como exposed the limitations of their pressing game. Opponents have found ways to bypass the first line, exploiting the gaps between United's forwards and midfielders before taking advantage of the space left behind.
 Bruno Fernandes questioned United's decision not to press man to man against Como, arguing that their opponents were being allowed too much time to build attacks. But simply increasing the intensity of the press is unlikely to provide the answer. United first need a defensive structure that the players can execute consistently.
 There were encouraging signs against Leeds, when Carrick's side looked more disciplined and compact despite being held to a 1-1 draw. A similar approach at Chelsea would make sense, with shorter distances between the defensive and midfield lines and better protection of central areas.
 United have spent just 56.5 minutes in a high defensive compactness structure this season, the 18th-lowest figure in the Premier League. Until they learn to defend collectively, their pressing ambitions will continue to leave them exposed.
 Bring Fernandes back into the starting XI 
 Carrick's decision to leave Fernandes on the bench against Bournemouth was a significant talking point, particularly after the United captain had questioned the team's tactics following their Champions League defeat to Como.
 The manager insisted that it was a football decision, but the absence of one of United's most influential players was difficult to overlook as they suffered another damaging defeat. Fernandes was not introduced even as the situation deteriorated, raising further questions about Carrick's decision.
 The pair have since held clear-the-air talks, with Carrick reiterating that Fernandes remains captain and that the club can move forward together.
 There is little doubt that the Portugal international has not consistently reached the levels he showed last season. Nor can United continue to rely on individual brilliance to compensate for their collective shortcomings. But his ability to create chances, progress possession and find decisive passes in transition remains vital.
 When United struggle to break down organised defences, Fernandes is often the player capable of producing something different. His influence in linking midfield and attack is particularly important for a side that has looked short of creativity and conviction.
 Carrick needs his best players on the pitch, especially when results are going against him. If Fernandes is fit and ready, leaving him out again would be difficult to justify.
 Give youth a chance 
 One of the more striking aspects of United's struggles is that several senior players who helped Carrick impress during his interim spell have failed to maintain those standards.
 That should encourage the manager to look beyond his established options. United have young players capable of injecting some much-needed energy into a team that has too often looked short of intensity.
 Harry Amass impressed during pre-season and deserves an opportunity to compete for a regular place at left-back, where United have struggled to find consistency.
 Shea Lacey is another option. The 19-year-old has had limited opportunities since scoring against Brighton in the Carabao Cup, but his willingness to take responsibility and make things happen could offer a different dimension to United's attack.

 Neither youngster should be expected to solve the team's problems overnight. Introducing inexperienced players into a struggling side carries its own risks, but continuing to rely on senior players who are not delivering is hardly a convincing alternative.
 The key is finding the right balance. Fernandes can provide the experience and quality, while the youngsters could bring the energy and enthusiasm that have been missing. Carrick must be prepared to trust the next generation if his established options continue to fall short.
 Constant reshuffling ain't helping 
 United's search for solutions has also resulted in too many players being moved around the pitch, making it difficult to establish consistent partnerships and a settled tactical identity.
 Diogo Dalot has featured at both right-back and left-back, while Leny Yoro has been deployed at right-back as well as centre-back. Mason Mount has operated on the right, and Youri Tielemans has been pushed into more advanced positions despite previously being viewed as a deeper-lying midfielder.
 Further forward, Matheus Cunha has been used on the left and through the middle, while Bryan Mbeumo has largely operated from the right despite producing some of his best football centrally last season.
 There have been understandable reasons for some of these adjustments, including injuries and the need to find a winning combination. Carrick's willingness to experiment was also one of the positives of his interim spell, particularly as United looked to move away from the limitations of Ruben Amorim's system.
 But tactical flexibility cannot come at the expense of clarity. Constant changes have made it difficult for players to develop an understanding of their roles and build partnerships on the pitch.
 Against Chelsea, Carrick needs to identify his strongest available XI and give players the best opportunity to perform in positions that suit their qualities. United do not necessarily need another tactical overhaul. They need a reliable foundation, a more coherent structure and players who understand their responsibilities.
 MICHAEL CARRICK
 MAN UNITED
